questions.q: Two numbers have HCF 12, LCM 480, and their sum is 156. Find the numbers.
questions.solution:
Write the numbers as 12a and 12b: a + b = 156/12 = 13 and ab = 480/12 = 40, so a, b = 5, 8 — the numbers are 60 and 96.

**Answer: 60 and 96**

questions.q: If sqrt{x+1} = 5 , then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Squaring both sides: x + 1 = 25, so x = 24.

**Answer: 24**

questions.q: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 72. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
The middle number is 72 ÷ 3 = 24, so the three numbers are 22, 24, 26 and the largest is 26.

**Answer: 26**

questions.q: What is the unit digit of 242 × 367 × 847?
questions.solution:
Only unit digits matter: 2 × 7 × 7 = 98, so the unit digit is 8.

**Answer: 8**

questions.q: The length of a rectangle is 12 cm. The diagonal of the rectangle is 13 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
Width = √(13² − 12²) = 5 cm (5-12-13 triple), so the area = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

**Answer: 60**

questions.q: Sum of the ages of two persons E and F is 50 years. The average age of E, F and G is 40 years. What is the age (in years) of G?
questions.solution:
E + F + G = 3 × 40 = 120 and E + F = 50, so G = 70 years.

**Answer: 70**

questions.q: X = 40 percent of 60 and Y = 50 percent of 40. What is the sum of X and Y?
An article is sold for a loss Rs. 98. Loss percentage is 28 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
28% of CP = Rs. 98 gives CP = Rs. 350, so SP = 350 − 98 = Rs. 252.

**Answer: Rs. 252**

questions.q: The profit earned on selling an article for Rs. 1200 is 9 times of the loss incurred on selling the same article for Rs. 1000. What will be the selling price of the article to earn a profit of 20 percent?
In an organisation, 30 percent employee are matriculates, 60 percent of remaining are graduates and now remaining 84 are post-graduates. What is the number of matriculates employee?
questions.solution:
After matriculates (30%), 60% of the remaining 70% are graduates, leaving 28% of the total as post-graduates: 0.28T = 84 → T = 300. Matriculates = 30% of 300 = 90.

**Answer: 90**

questions.q: A, B and C working alone can complete a work in 8, 12 and 24 days respectively. In how many days A, B and C together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
One-day rates over 24: 3/24 + 2/24 + 1/24 = 6/24 = 1/4 of the work per day, so together they need 4 days.

**Answer: 4**

questions.q: Q and R together are 2 times as efficient as P. P and R together are 1.5 times as efficient as Q. Q and R together can complete a work in 90 days. P alone can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
Q and R together are twice as efficient as P, so P's rate = (1/90)/2 = 1/180, and P alone needs 180 days.

**Answer: 180**

questions.q: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. Length of each train is 165 metres. They cross each other in 15 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of each train?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = (165 + 165)/15 = 22 m/s for the two trains together, so each train runs at 11 m/s.

**Answer: 11**

questions.q: A bus starts moving with the initial speed of 20 km/hr. Its speed increases by 10 km/hr after every hour. How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 270 km?
questions.solution:
Hourly distances are 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 km, cumulatively 20, 50, 90, 140, 200, 270 — the 270 km mark is reached after 6 hours.

**Answer: 6**

questions.q: A person sells 20 articles at Rs. 60 per article after giving 15 percent discount. He earns a profit of 30 percent. If no discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
MP = 60/0.85 ≈ 70.59 and CP = 60/1.3 ≈ 46.15, so without the discount the profit = (70.59 − 46.15)/46.15 ≈ 52.94 percent.

**Answer: 52.94 percent**
